origin_result.basis: Final manufacture in UAE: PASS; minimal operations: PASS; CTH: PASS (all 2 non-originating inputs classified outside heading 9403); VA: PASS (build-down 52.0% against threshold 40%, FOB basis).

procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism requires the factory to be registered through its Factory Registration service before applying for a certificate of origin; registration takes about 3 working days and the factory must be located outside a free zone.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The issuing authority requires the application to include the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product, and each item must qualify separately; it may also ask for detailed cost sheets and conduct a factory visit.

The Ministry of Foreign Trade provides the 'Certificate of Origin for India' e-service; the exporter logs in, chooses the service, fills in the application form, uploads the required documents, and submits the application.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 for an invoice value up to AED 100,000 (the fee band for the given shipment value).
The Ministry of Foreign Trade approves the application or returns it with comments for correction; the exporter prints the approved certificate.

The competent authority issues the certificate prior to, at, or within five working days of export; it is valid for twelve months from issue and covers only one import. A certificate may be issued retrospectively up to 12 months from the date of shipment, marked 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9 of India's certificate form.

The exporter ensures the goods are shipped directly from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, or storage. If a third party issues the invoice, the exporter indicates 'third-party invoicing'.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and holds origin information, including which origin criterion is claimed; the importer must answer a customs request within 10 working days.
The exporter keeps origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years starting from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue.

caveats.note: The '+' in the rule 'CTH + VA 40%' is interpreted by Mansha as requiring both the tariff shift and the value addition to be met; the agreement does not define '+'.
The origin determination (final manufacture, minimal operations, CTH, VA) is based on the exporter's own declaration.
Factory declared in a free zone: likely not eligible for the ministry's factory registration; confirm with the ministry.
The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty only; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge, and any anti-dumping or safeguard duties still apply.
The duty estimate is based on the shipment value given; India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value, so actual amounts will differ.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
The certificate fee estimate assumes the invoice value equals the shipment value given.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement, which may affect the value addition calculation.
The agreement does not specify whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
The certificate form box for remarks: the agreement says box 8, but India's form says box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
The issuing authority may require detailed cost sheets and a factory visit when applying.
UAE law sets a 3-year record-keeping minimum, but the CEPA requires 5 years for CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is from secondary sources, not the official text.
The 40% value-added letter required for factory registration is a registration condition only, not the CEPA product-specific rule test.
The factory registration requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, so a free-zone producer may not be eligible.

follow_up_questions: Is the factory located in a free zone? If so, it may not be eligible for the required factory registration, which is a prerequisite for the certificate of origin.
